problem: "legalize" rendered as "legitimize": different meaning (give legal form vs. confer legitimacy).
replacement: Nor have the Americans ever supposed that one consequence of democratic principles is the overthrow of marital power or the confusion of the natural authorities within the family. They hold that every association must have a head if it is to achieve its purpose, and that the natural head of the conjugal association is the man. They therefore do not deny him the right to direct his partner. They maintain that in the small association of husband and wife, as in the great social community, the object of democracy is to regulate and legalize the powers that are necessary, not to overthrow all power. This opinion is not held by one sex and disputed by the other. I never observed that the women of America regard conjugal authority as a fortunate usurpation of their rights, or that they thought themselves degraded by submitting to it. It seemed to me, on the contrary, that they take a kind of pride in the voluntary surrender of their own will, and make it their boast to bend to the yoke rather than shake it off. Such at least is the feeling expressed by the most virtuous of their sex; the others stay silent; and in the United States it is not the practice for a guilty wife to clamor for the rights of women while she tramples on her holiest duties.

problem: "considered as seductive but imperfect beings" became "treated as": shifts a judgment of opinion into behavior.
replacement: It has often been remarked that in Europe a certain contempt lurks even in the flattery men lavish on women. A European often pretends to be woman’s slave, yet it can be seen that he never sincerely thinks her his equal. In the United States men seldom pay compliments to women, but every day they show how much they esteem them. They constantly display complete confidence in a wife’s understanding and deep respect for her freedom. They have decided that her mind is as fit as a man’s to discover plain truth, and her heart as firm in embracing it; and they have never tried to shelter her virtue, any more than his, behind prejudice, ignorance, and fear. In Europe, where man so easily submits to the despotic sway of women, it seems that women are nonetheless cut off from some of the greatest qualities of the human species and regarded as seductive but imperfect beings. And, what may well provoke astonishment, women in the end see themselves in the same light, and almost regard it as a privilege that they are entitled to show themselves frivolous, feeble, and timid. The women of America claim no such privileges.

problem: Restructured sentence makes "I do not hesitate to say" govern the confinement of women instead of the concession ("although...") followed by his avowal that he has seen no loftier position.
replacement: So the Americans do not believe that man and woman have the duty or the right to do the same things. They do, however, hold both of their roles in equal regard, and although the two lots differ, they treat the two as beings of equal worth. They do not give woman’s courage the same form or direction as man’s, but they never doubt that she has it. And if they think a man and his partner should not always use their intellect and understanding in the same way, they at least believe her understanding to be as sound as his, and her intellect as clear. Thus, while leaving woman’s social inferiority in place, they have done everything they could to raise her morally and intellectually to the level of man. In this respect they seem to me to have grasped the true principle of democratic improvement remarkably well. For my part, I do not hesitate to say that, although the women of the United States are confined within the narrow circle of domestic life, and their situation is in some respects one of extreme dependence, I have nowhere seen woman hold a loftier position. And suppose I were asked, now that I am near the end of this work, in which I have described so many important things the Americans have done, what the singular prosperity and growing strength of that people should chiefly be credited to. I would answer: to the superiority of their women.
